text.p: Chelsea Clinton turned 17 on Thursday, having come a long way since the day four years ago when she and her father turned loose her pet turtle as one of her last acts before coming to Washington.

She celebrated in relative low-key fashion, going to classes as usual at Sidwell Friends, an exclusive private school where she is in her senior year. She planned to have a private dinner with some of her friends later.
The big celebration of her birthday comes this weekend, when parents President Bill Clinton and Hillary Rodham Clinton take her to New York to see some shows.
"They're going to go up, they're going to take in some shows, they'll probably have some meals and have some fun. I think I'll leave it at that," White House spokesman Mike McCurry said.
In March she plans to accompany her mother on a tour of several African countries during her spring break from school.
Keenly interested in ballet and dance, Chelsea does not appear to be trying to follow her father's footsteps into politics.
White House officials familiar with her studies say she is showing an interest in taking pre-med classes when she starts college next autumn.

She has visited a variety of Ivy League schools, including Harvard University in Boston, Brown University in Providence, Rhode Island, and Yale University in New Haven, Connecticut, as well as Stanford in Palo Alto, California.
President Clinton has said Chelsea had not decided on a school in response to a Los Angeles Times report that she had been accepted by Harvard.
